(prior-agent validation of the v6 detector against real device telemetry, branch

This is a pre-existing v5-era live/replay divergence, unchanged by v6. Not included in the fixture: testing 'absence' here would only prove 'still absent, same as v5' and would NOT exercise any v6-specific max-dwell/progress-gate/episode-identity logic. Documented here rather than given a dedicated window per the task's explicit option to omit.

windows.label: unwind_10_07_56
windows.assertion: This is the 10:07.56 driver-rescue anchor -- NOT one of the 7 keeps in report section A (it is the extra 'driver-rescue anchor extras' the task asks for). confidence 0.95, driver_assisted_unwind True, driver_causation 'driverCreated', AND driver_assist_raw_torque_only True (the one anchor of the 4 rescue anchors where the assist confirmed via raw torque without steering_pressed). Window is asymmetric (~13s back) because this episode arms at mono 663.17 -- 11.9s before the deficit is flagged -- and both crown timestamps and the rebound land inside that long arm-to-deficit span, not near occurred_mono_time itself; this is the report's own sanity-check example (section 'Sanity check (Step 1)') of high_angle_unwind_scale peaking near 1.0 around mono 307.6-307.8 and 357.9-358.2 in the OTHER two rebound windows, and analogously dynamic here. NOTE (adversarial-review Fix 3, updated post-review): rebound_start_mono_time/rebound_duration_s revised from the original report's 664.396409/1.9653 -- the pre-fix rebound tracker armed on this episode's very FIRST below-tolerance sample (near arm, 663.170414) with no check that old-direction torque had ever genuinely been held first; from 663.17-664.35 requested_torque is decaying but stays on the NEW-direction side of neutral the whole time (old_direction_component pinned at its 0.0 floor), so 664.396409 was actually the FIRST sample the component ever reached CROWN_NEUTRAL_TOLERANCE (a hold beginning, not a release-then-rebound), and got misattributed as a rebound onset. Fix 3 requires a genuine prior hold (component >= tolerance) before arming the rebound tracker, so tracking now correctly starts at 664.58729 (the next dip back below tolerance after that hold); rebound_max_magnitude (0.9711, the real peak at mono 674.607) is unaffected since it occurs long after either candidate start.

windows.label: reject_06_38_9_never_enters_dwell

anti_vacuity_probe.description: Track detector.turn_stop_episode.state transitions across the window. A 'moving' episode begins essentially AT the anchor (mono 466.359) and transitions to 'slowing' at 466.448, but NO 'dwell' state is entered anywhere near the anchor -- the episode lingers in 'slowing' and only belatedly reaches a brief (0.089s) 'dwell' far away at mono 470.948-471.037, well outside any reasonable proximity to the anchor.

windows.assertion: No turnStopTurn fires anywhere in the window. The anti-vacuity guard proves this is NOT vacuous by confirming the episode DOES become active (moving/slowing) right at the anchor -- it just never forms a dwell there -- distinguishing this from a case where the detector saw no activity at all.

windows.label: reject_08_33_7_center_band_reset

anti_vacuity_probe.description: A real dwell IS entered (proving the state machine reached 'dwell', not silently absent) at mono 581.808 (angle -11.9deg), but resets directly to None (episode discarded) after ~1.1s at mono 582.907 when the wheel drifts back inside the center band with no meaningful demand (DESIGN S2 rule 4) -- the state trace goes 'dwell' -> None directly, NEVER passing through 'released', so no PendingTurnStopCandidate is ever created from this episode.

windows.assertion: No turnStopTurn fires anywhere in the window. The anti-vacuity guard proves the detector actually ENTERS 'dwell' (dwell_start ~581.808, duration ~1.0997s matching the report's '~1.1s') and confirms it exits directly to no-episode (never 'released'), i.e. this is the center-band-drift-reset mechanism specifically, not a generic absence.

windows.label: cooldown_pair_731_977_735_289
windows.assertion: 731.977 is a genuinely NEW v6-only turnStopTurn (absent in the v5 replay) that fires and consumes the shared 8s per-type EVENT_COOLDOWN. 735.289 (dwell physically happens at 734.277-735.289, pre-progress 496.4deg, post-progress growing to 109.2deg by its own 2.1s deadline at 737.389 -- comfortably clearing BOTH progress gates) does NOT fire, purely because 737.389 - 731.977 = 5.41s < 8.0s EVENT_COOLDOWN. This is the ALREADY-ACCEPTED amendment A10 tradeoff ('cooldown-consumed episodes... not new-discard-rule losses'), not a bug and not a gate failure. Do not assert 735.289 fires (it correctly doesn't); do not omit it silently either -- assert its absence explicitly with this documented cause.
windows.note: Window intentionally does NOT need to include the earlier 723.690 keep: 731.977 is its OWN cooldown chain-setter (731.977 - 723.690 = 8.287s > 8.0s, already clear regardless), so only 731.977's own ~0.7s of lead-in is required. Verified empirically that starting earlier (~723-728) truncates an unrelated earlier episode mid-flight and produces a spurious extra detection -- avoided by keeping the window this tight.

short_dwell_population_doc: Report section C: 25 v5 turnStopTurn total minus the 5 long-dwell rejects = 20 short-dwell (0.3-1.6s, 42-486deg) events. 19/20 fire under v6 (the 19 turn_stop_keep windows above); the 20th (v5 anchor mono 735.289, dwell 1.012s/116.6deg) does NOT fire, but NOT because of the pre/post-progress gates -- see the cooldown_pair_731_977_735_289 window/assertion above for the full mechanism.
old_manifest_decodability_doc: A separate test (test_old_v5_manifest_lines_still_decode_safely in test_route94_replay.py) constructs 3-4 SYNTHESIZED manifest-shaped dicts (route/event/git identifiers replaced with fixed test strings per amendment A11 -- no real device identifiers are committed) matching the STRUCTURE of a real v5-era manifest line, and does a schema-level capnp round-trip decode check (LateralPayload / DrivingEvent) confirming version<3 / detector_version 2-5 style records decode safely with group_role defaulting to 'primary' and no v6-only fields expected. A full driving_event_indexer.py integration (tmp_path segment trees, real scan_once/rebuild) was judged too heavy for this fixture-focused test file; the schema-level check directly exercises the append-only guarantee this fixture's own v6 records rely on.
